_comment: Machine-ready per-flag schema for common git commands and daily-use flags.

commands.name: git init
commands.notes: --bare repositories have no working tree; used for remotes.

commands.name: git clone
commands.notes: --depth reduces fetched history; use git fetch --unshallow to expand.

commands.name: git add
commands.notes: Use git status --porcelain to inspect index vs working tree.

commands.name: git mv
commands.notes: git mv is convenience; equivalent manual steps: mv && git add new && git rm old.

commands.name: git restore
commands.notes: Replaces older 'git checkout -- <file>' pattern for file restores.

commands.name: git rm
commands.notes: --cached useful to stop tracking files while keeping local copy.

commands.name: git commit
commands.notes: Amending and force-pushing is common but dangerous on shared branches—use --force-with-lease.

commands.name: git status
commands.notes: Porcelain output is recommended for GUIs and scripts.

commands.name: git diff
commands.notes: Useful for generating patches (git diff > file.patch).

commands.name: git log
commands.notes: Common UI display: --graph --decorate --oneline --all

commands.name: git show
commands.notes: Can inspect blobs and tree objects directly via commit:path.

commands.name: git branch
commands.notes: Use git switch -c or git checkout -b to create+switch.

commands.name: git checkout
commands.notes: Prefer git switch and git restore for clarity.

commands.name: git switch
commands.notes: Clearer separation between switching and restoring files.

commands.name: git merge

flags.label: Create a merge commit even if fast-forward
Squash commits into working tree changes (no commit)

commands.notes: When conflicts occur, resolve files, git add them, then git commit (or git merge --continue).

commands.name: git rebase
commands.notes: Rewriting shared history requires force-push (use --force-with-lease).

commands.name: git cherry-pick
commands.description: Apply a commit from another branch onto current branch.
commands.notes: Use -x for traceability when backporting fixes.

commands.name: git revert

flags.label: Parent number for reverting a merge

commands.notes: Preferred safe method to undo public commits.

commands.name: git tag
commands.notes: Annotated tags are recommended for release tagging (support messages and signing).

commands.name: git fetch
commands.notes: Fetch only updates remote-tracking branches; you must merge/rebase/checkout to incorporate changes.

commands.name: git pull
commands.notes: Consider using fetch + manual merge/rebase for safer workflows.

commands.name: git push
commands.notes: Prefer --force-with-lease over --force when rewriting history.

commands.name: git remote
commands.notes: Use git remote -v to confirm fetch/push URLs.

commands.name: git ls-remote
commands.notes: Useful in scripts to inspect remote refs before cloning or pushing.

commands.name: git credential
commands.notes: Better to configure OS credential managers (manager-core) rather than storing plain text.

commands.name: git stash
commands.notes: Stashes are referenced by stash@{n}; use git stash show -p stash@{1} to view the patch.

commands.name: git apply
commands.notes: git apply is for working-tree patch application; use git am for mailbox->commits.

commands.name: git bisect
commands.notes: Bisection requires deterministic tests; use git bisect run to automate.

commands.name: git grep
commands.notes: Use in scripts; e.g., git grep -l pattern | xargs ...

commands.name: git clean
commands.notes: Use -n first to preview removals; -x deletes ignored files including config—use with caution.

commands.name: git archive
commands.notes: Useful to produce release snapshots.

commands.name: git bundle
commands.notes: Transfer repository offline by creating bundle, copying, then cloning/applying.

commands.name: git submodule

flags.label: Run command in submodules
flags.example: git submodule foreach 'git pull origin main'

commands.notes: Using --recurse-submodules on clone reduces surprises when submodules are present.

commands.name: git worktree
commands.notes: Worktrees share object DB but have separate working directories.

commands.name: git config
commands.notes: Many credentials and pull behaviors are configured here (e.g., credential.helper, pull.rebase).

commands.name: git describe

flags.label: Show abbreviated SHA if no tag

commands.notes: Useful to generate build versions and release names.

commands.name: git daemon
commands.notes: Generally replaced by SSH/HTTP(S) hosting; exposing daemon requires caution.

commands.name: git reset

flags.label: Move HEAD only; keep index & working tree
Default: move HEAD and unstage changes

commands.notes: --hard will delete uncommitted changes. Use with care.

commands.name: git reflog
commands.notes: Use reflog to find previous HEAD after accidental reset --hard.

commands.name: git filter-branch / git filter-repo
commands.notes: History rewriting is destructive—coordinate with collaborators and prefer git-filter-repo.

commands.name: git cherry
commands.notes: Useful to evaluate commits unique to a branch.

commands.name: git format-patch
commands.notes: Used in email-based workflows; pair with git am at the receiver.

commands.name: git am
commands.notes: Common for applying emailed patches.

commands.name: git rerere
commands.notes: Helpful when repeatedly rebasing/merging the same conflicts.

commands.name: git shortlog
commands.notes: Useful for CONTRIBUTORS or release notes.

commands.name: git fsck
commands.notes: Often run on server/backups to verify health.

commands.name: git verify-pack
commands.notes: Used to diagnose pack bloat before prune/gc.

commands.name: git count-objects
commands.notes: Quick repo size diagnostics.

commands.name: git prune

flags.label: Expire objects older than given time

commands.notes: Dangerous on backups; ensure you have refs and backups before pruning.

commands.name: git gc

flags.label: Prune unreachable objects older than time

commands.notes: Used for scheduled server maintenance; can be slow and disk-heavy.

commands.name: git whatchanged
commands.notes: Replaced by git log --name-status --pretty=...
